text:
erin: Heads-up — tonight 23:30 UTC we'll preemptively drain a small cohort in us-west1 (rack-r7) to mitigate an egress queue surge we've been seeing on az6. Plan: staggered node drains + warm KV seeding. Expected impact: ~5-10% throughput degradation for ~45m. Will monitor latency and roll back if p95 > 150ms. @oncall please ack. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sam: Ack. I'll own traffic shift and backfill. Can we compress warm-kv to 10m?
erin: Prefer 15m to be safe — 10m is possible if we run aggressive kv-seed and preheat prefixes, but higher chance of cold-cache errors.
leo: Suggest a canary: drain 2 nodes first (node03, node07), wait 10m, validate error budget & queue depth, then proceed. I'll queue the egress-ratecap to 100mbps for the cohort during the window.
maya: Cost FYI — if we burst for warmbackfill and use spot replacements we'll hit an incremental ~$1.2k for the window (short estimate).
infra-bot: [schedule] maintenance created: id=mn-usw1-2024-1705554321, window=23:30-00:20 UTC, owner=erin.
sam: I'll draft the customer notice after we lock the start time and canary step.
erin: Quick ops checklist (will paste to runbook at start):
```
# cordon + drain canary nodes
kubectl cordon node/rack-r7-node03
kubectl drain node/rack-r7-node03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# warm kv seed (redis)
redis-cli -h kv-seed-usw1 --eval seed_kv.lua 50000
# toggle egress ratecap (maint API)
oc-apply route-config --cohort rack-r7 --egress-cap 100mbps
```
erin: Note: keep `--grace-period` low for canary to surface long-tail latencies early.
leo: Adding a quick smoke script after canary drain: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMOKE_TOKEN" https://api.us-west1.redwood.ai/healthz?mode=smoke` — check 200s and token auth times.
maya: Also toggle alert thresholds: raise p50->150ms, p95->200ms while we do the warm seed so transient alert storms don't page. We'll revert thresholds after stabilization.
sam: Oncall runbook pointers: if error rate >0.5% rollback by re-introducing the drained nodes and disabling egress ratecap. Who will run rollback? @leo?
leo: I'll be standing by for rollback, but prefer to throttle back steps first (pause bulk drain) and increase canary sample.
erin: Communications plan:
- 23:00 UTC: internal heads-up to #customer-notice-drafts (sam)
- 23:20 UTC: short reminder in #oncall and #eng-status
- 23:35 UTC: update after canary check
- 00:20 UTC: post completion summary + perf graph snippet
sam: I'll send customer-facing short note: "There will be a brief maintenance starting 23:30 UTC in US-West to improve network stability; some requests may see slightly higher latency." Keep it non-technical.
infra-bot: [incident-prep] runbook pinned: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-drain-preemptive
erin: Small data point — current egress queue depth on rack-r7 averaged 74% for last 3h with occasional spikes to 96% which triggered our smoothing alarms. We need this to avoid larger throttles later.
leo: Also adjust routing policy to prefer regional-fallback after canary: `route-policy set rack-r7 latency:fallback=small-variant`
maya: Confirming budget owner ok with the estimated cost. I've logged a quick charge code: ENG-MAINT-2024-07.
sam: Oncall acked and I'll be online at start. tagging SRE shift: @oncall-sre
erin: Great — final checklist: 1) canary nodes identified (node03,node07) 2) warm seed scripts ready 3) ratecap config staged 4) customer notice queued 5) rollback owner assigned (leo). If anything slips say so now.
sam: All set from my side. :thumbsup:
leo: Ready. Standing by from 23:20 UTC.
maya: Ready — will monitor billing/charge push.
erin: Thanks team, will kick at 23:30. Posting runtime updates in-thread. :rocket:
